description: REQ-G2's field-equality check (step 3, lines 464-474) specifies amount comparison precision only for two unit systems: 'exact equality for amount_jpy, ≤ 0.01 USDC epsilon for amount_usdc'. The spec earlier (verification-architecture.md line 146) explicitly anticipates on-chain settlements via 'on-chain `eth_getLogs` for ERC-20 Transfer to founder wallet' as a payout-endpoint-allowlist entry, and the broader project context (founder wallets on Base + Solana, per the human-funded earn track) involves at minimum: USDC on Base (ERC-20, 6 decimals, raw units in uint256 wei), SOL transfers (9 decimals, lamports as uint64), and potentially other tokens. The spec is silent on (i) which unit system the on-chain `amount_*` field in the event row uses (raw wei/lamports as integer vs. human-decimal float), (ii) what epsilon applies (10000 raw units = 0.01 USDC on Base if comparing 6-decimal wei to float; exact integer equality for lamports?), (iii) whether the JSON-path extraction from `eth_getLogs` response (which yields hex-encoded `data` and 32-byte topic arrays) is parsed identically across runner re-fetch and skill emission. The result is undefined behavior at the precise tier the founder-wallet ROI dashboard depends on: an on-chain attacker could submit `amount_usdc: 0.005` (= 5000 raw units, below the 0.01 float epsilon but above zero in integer space), the runner re-fetches `eth_getLogs`, parses `data` as a uint256, compares against `event.amount_usdc` — and the comparison succeeds within epsilon for a non-existent payout if the runner parses raw and the skill emits float. PROP-G2-runtime fixture corpus (PROP-G2-runtime line 90) names 3 specific attacks but none involve on-chain logs; the 20 random rejections may or may not include lamport/wei cases. Required fix: extend REQ-G2 step 3 to enumerate per-platform comparison rules in `payout-endpoint-allowlist.json` itself: each allowlist entry must declare the unit system (`jpy_int | usdc_float_6dp | wei_uint256 | lamport_uint64 | …`) AND the comparison predicate (`exact | epsilon:<value-in-declared-unit>`). The runner SHALL convert both event-row value and re-fetched response value to the declared canonical unit before comparing. PROP-G2-runtime fixture corpus MUST include at minimum one ERC-20 `eth_getLogs` fixture (real Transfer log + matching event row + correct integer-unit comparison) AND one off-by-one-wei attack (event claims 1 USDC, log shows 999999 raw units = 0.999999 USDC; runner MUST reject under exact integer equality and not pass under float epsilon). Without this, the 3-check pattern that closes ROUND-2-001 for JPY-and-Stripe-USDC payouts has a quiet hole for the on-chain payouts the project explicitly intends to support.

evidence.snippet: - `amount_jpy` (or `amount_usdc`) appears in the response at a platform-defined JSON path AND its numeric value equals the event row's value (exact equality for amount_jpy, ≤ 0.01 USDC epsilon for amount_usdc);
